scores.rationale: Mostly correct on Redis Lua atomicity, ONNX, LightGBM missing values and time-split labels. Minor imprecision remains, such as fail-open on stand-in and the concurrent-duplicate ZADD claim, but none affects the design.

scores.rationale: Solves inline issuer fraud scoring with explicit exclusions and reasons, resolves ambiguity with defaults, and is buildable by a 5-person team. Deferring 3DS step-up is a minor gap.

scores.rationale: Data ownership, sole writers and consistency are explicit, and choices are applied consistently across sections. Only tiny loose ends remain.

scores.rationale: Covers domain-meaningful alerts, blue/green deployment, rollback times, named ownership, runbooks and migrations, sized to the team. A 24/7 on-call for 4 engineers is a slight stretch.

Each decision carries a reversibility rating and a revisit trigger. The hard choices (contract, PAN, language) are validated early by spikes, and the vendor cancellation is flagged as the only point of no return.

scores.evidence: There is no stream processor in v1.
scores.rationale: Starts simple with Redis Lua and in-process ONNX, defers Flink, a UI and multi-region, and gives triggers for each. The components are all justified.

checklist.evidence: p99 ≤ 50 ms server-side at 1,000 TPS... One Redis `EVALSHA` ... ≤ 20 ms
**Fail open** on timeout, deferring to the processor stand-in... fail closed only for high-risk merchant categories
The Decision Service, the Velocity Updater and the Replay Harness all use it.
The most recent 90 days are excluded from training because their labels haven't matured.
Value detection rate at the target false-positive ratio... Choosing the operating point... business trade-off between losses, false declines and analyst capacity
A reply of NO writes a fraud label and opens a case asking an analyst to block the card.
PAN: **never present**. The request contract has no PAN field, and a CI check plus a log scrubber reject 13–19-digit strings
The consumer is idempotent because of the member encoding... Kafka key `card_token`; Redis rebuilt from Kafka
daily population stability index on the top 20 features and on the score... `champion` slot and an optional `challenger` slot
DecisionEvent contains the full request, every feature value used, the outcome of every rule... the versions
At least 3 instances across 3 AZs... designed to 1,000 sustained and 2,000 burst

traps.evidence: Only inline scoring prevents loss (#3). Asynchronous-only catches fraud after the money is gone.
after 20 ms, skip it... the Authorization Service times out at 100 ms and fails open to its own checks plus processor rules
Trains LightGBM with a time-based split. The most recent 90 days are excluded
Train it on features made by replaying history through the same feature code the live service uses.
Use card tokens only, never the PAN (full card number), to keep PCI scope small.

note: An exceptionally thorough, well-reasoned plan with explicit assumptions, spikes and reversibility. Weaknesses are limited step-up actions, a thin 3DS/OTP path, ungrounded costs, and a hard p99 budget for a very low-latency Lua call.
